research_scope: Five complete categorical reviews, including size-scope corrections for pullbacks, filtered categories and adjunctions; no research or new meanings.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed all full source mathematical text and effective references, preserving the difference between arbitrary and small categories, terminal/final universal clauses versus prerequisite diagram structures, filteredness axioms, adjunction naturality and fibres over base objects.
amendments.reason: Source-free contextual review of categorical universal structures, correcting restrictive small-category reference links without adding source material or aliases.

references.context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
references.matching_note: Source occurrence 'category C' denotes an ordinary category without a smallness requirement. Existing small-category meaning is too restrictive; do not conflate a fibred category, groupoid or slice category with the ambient category.
references.reason: The existing generic category meaning explicitly assumes smallness, not warranted here.

references.context: Category theory: pair of coproduct cocone legs i:X→P,j:Y→P from two specified objects to a common vertex P, independent of whether P satisfies universal coproduct property.
references.reason: The compatible pair of injections is structural data used before asserting their universality.
references.matching_note: The arrows are not generally monomorphisms in an arbitrary category.

references.disposition: Unique existence of h making h∘i=f and h∘j=g for every f,g is the defining universal property of the binary coproduct; no additional pre-existing 'unique-map' concept is assumed.
Composition equations are already ordinary operations in the ambient category.

references.context: Category theory: ordinary (possibly nonsmall) category with objects, identities, morphisms and associative composition; the definition of pullbacks does not restrict C to be small.
references.reason: The indexed meaning of a small category incorrectly imposes set-sized object collection on an arbitrary categorical pullback.
references.matching_note: Scope correction to general category, not a new source or definition.

references.phrase: commuting cone to arrows X→S and Y→S
references.context: Category theory: compatible cone over a cospan f:X→S, g:Y→S, consisting of arrows p:P→X,q:P→Y with fp=gq; P not necessarily a pullback.
references.reason: The compatible cone is prerequisite diagram data separate from the pullback's universal property.
references.matching_note: Keep direction opposite to pushout cocones and distinct from pseudocones with invertible 2-cells.

references.disposition: Unique mediating morphism from every compatible cone to P is the defining universal property of a pullback; do not introduce a self-dependent universal pullback as a prerequisite.
These are equalities between composites in the category, not new conditions of invertibility.

references.context: Category theory: an ordinary category I with objects, arrows, identities and composition; smallness is not explicitly stipulated by the filtered-category axioms in this source.
references.reason: The linked small-category meaning imposes a size condition not present in the formulation.
references.matching_note: Keep general category candidate distinct from small indexed categories in later audit.

references.context: Category theory: two parallel arrows u,v:i→j in a category with the same domain i and codomain j; equality after postcomposition j→k is the filteredness condition.
references.reason: Parallel arrows are a reusable diagram shape distinct from equalizing them.
references.matching_note: Keep the parallel-pair structure apart from the axiom that it eventually coequalizes.

references.disposition: Requiring an object k with arrows i→k and j→k for each pair of objects i,j is a defining axiom of filteredness. The existential requirement must not become a recursively presupposed property.

references.phrase: after an arrow j→k, u and v become equal
references.disposition: The specified equalization of parallel arrows is a separate requirement from a common upper object; all three axioms are present.

references.phrase: functors L:C to D and R:D to C
references.context: Category theory: two ordinary covariant functors between categories C and D, L:C→D and R:D→C, with no specified smallness; neither is a contravariant functor.
references.reason: Earlier small-source-and-target category functor meaning is more restrictive than the general adjunction formula.
references.matching_note: Correction preserves covariance and dual domain/codomain directions.

references.phrase: bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C
references.context: Category theory: family of hom-set bijections Hom_D(LX,Y)≅Hom_C(X,RY), indexed by X∈C,Y∈D, with each hom class set-valued under needed local-smallness conventions.
references.reason: Adjunction uses bijections of hom collections and functorial compatibility; these are reusable categorical components.
references.matching_note: Do not infer an object-level isomorphism LX≅RY or ignore naturality.

references.phrase: natural in both X and Y
references.context: Category theory: naturality of a family of hom-set bijections in variables X and Y, commuting with morphisms in C and D; the X-variable is contravariant in both hom functors.
references.reason: Naturality in each variable is mathematically stronger than independent pointwise bijections.
references.matching_note: Audit alongside natural transformations/2-variable natural isomorphism without identifying with plain bijection.

references.disposition: The two functors run in opposite directions between C and D, but neither is assumed contravariant.

references.matching_note: A fibred category with groupoid fibres is the immediate parent meaning.
Every fibre E_U is discrete, with only identity arrows.

references.context: Category theory: ordinary functor p:E→C from total category E to base category C, without requiring source or target categories to be small.
references.reason: The fibred category structure is organized over an ordinary functor between potentially large categories.
references.matching_note: Compare with size-unrestricted functor candidate from adjunction/presheaf contexts.

references.context: Category theory: fibre category E_U of functor p:E→C over object U∈C, consisting of objects x with p(x)=U and arrows α between them with p(α)=id_U.
references.reason: The fibre-category construction is independently reusable when requiring all fibres be discrete.
references.matching_note: Keep fibre of a category-over-base distinct from topological fibres and tensor products.
